                      [32m"isActive: 'boolean',\n"[39m +

                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'user({ isActive: true }) // ❌ Error: "Email is required when user is active"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'user({ isActive: false }) // ✅ Valid\n'[39m +

                      [32m`import { type as arktype } from "arktype"; import { FormBuilder, useFormBuilder } from "@arktype-form-builder/core"; const user = arktype({ name: arktype("string > 0").configure({ label: "Name", }), email: arktype("string > 0").configure({ label: "E-mail", }), "category?": arktype("'admin' | 'staff'"), });\n`[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# standard-schema/packages/spec/README.md at main · standard-schema/standard-schema\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-04-08, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/standard-schema/standard-schema/blob/main/packages/spec/README.md)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Schemas libraries that want to support Standard Schema must implement the `StandardSchemaV1` interface.\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Transcript: Standard Schema: The Universal JavaScript Data Interface\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-02-03, last updated: 2026-06-06, [Read more](https://syntax.fm/show/873/standard-schema-the-universal-javascript-data-interface/transcript)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Authors created standard schema to standardize data validation\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Validate data to catch errors when data changes unexpectedly\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Standard schema doesn't replace existing libraries, it standardizes validation\n"[39m +
                      [32m'- Standard schema standardizes validate method inputs and outputs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Standard schema avoids need for numerous library-to-library adapters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Libraries handle errors, standard schema just validates\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"So a a schema, if you haven't done done this before, is you describe what your data looks like.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"And when you have a piece of data, you can validate it against the schema to make sure that it looks like what you're expecting.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"So the idea with standard schema is it's not a way to define what your data looks like.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'So what they have agreed is a standard way to define several things.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'First of all, how to actually validate the data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"So what's standard schema does is anyone who implements standard schema will simply tack on this tilde standard onto each of the schemas.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"First of all, I wanna be able to call the validate method on your schema, and I don't care who has made it.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"I'm just gonna call a validate method on that schema, and then that validate method will be called and will be able to return data in a structured way."[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# There are too many JavaScript schema libraries, so support only one\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-06-10, last updated: 2026-06-25, [Read more](https://www.inngest.com/blog/too-many-javascript-schema-libraries-support-only-one)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Standard Schema is not a new schema language, validation library, or syntax users have to learn.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Users still write Zod, Valibot, ArkType, Yup, or whatever else they already chose.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Standard Schema is only the small compatibility interface those schema objects expose so other libraries can validate unknown input and recover input/output types without knowing which schema library produced them.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Schema libraries implement it, libraries like ours consume it, and users never see it.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Zod, Valibot, ArkType, Yup, Joi, and others already support `~standard`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'vendor: "inngest",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schema: TSchema,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'data: unknown,\n'[39m +
                      [32m') {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const result = await schema["~standard"].validate(data);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`validate()` can return a result directly or return a `Promise`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The schema implementation decides, so any code that calls `validate()` has to account for both.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`validate()` returns `{value} | {issues} | Promise<...>`, so the signature makes validation failures look like returned values, not thrown errors.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Standard Schema standardizes the successful and failed validation result shapes, but it does not make validator execution safe.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Validators are still userland code, and userland code can throw.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Claude Code for Standard Schema — Workflow Guide\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-04-18, last updated: 2026-04-26, [Read more](https://claudecodeguides.com/claude-code-for-standard-schema-workflow-guide/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You are using the Standard Schema specification to write validator-agnostic code that works with Zod, Valibot, ArkType, or any compliant validation library.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Standard Schema defines a common interface so libraries, frameworks, and tools can accept any validator without coupling to a specific one.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Standard Schema defines `~standard.validate()` as the universal validation method.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Spec: Standard Schema (validator-agnostic interface)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Standard Schema Rules\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Library/framework code uses StandardSchema interface, not Zod\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Validate with: schema['~standard'].validate(data)\n"[39m +
                      [32m'- Type inference: InferOutput<typeof schema>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Claude Code should define `createForm<T extends StandardSchema>(schema: T)` that uses `schema['~standard'].validate(data)` for validation, infers the form data type with `InferOutput<T>`, checks `result.issues` for validation errors, and does not import any specific validation library.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"1. **Using `~standard` wrong in type checks.** Claude accesses `schema['~standard']` at the type level instead of the value level.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'The `~standard` property is a runtime value with `validate()` — use it for validation calls, not type narrowing.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Standard Schema: TypeScript Validation Interop 2026\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-03-25, last updated: 2026-06-21, [Read more](https://www.pkgpulse.com/guides/standard-schema-typescript-validation-interop-2026)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- **Standard Schema is a spec, not a library** — it's a TypeScript interface that validation libraries implement via a `~standard` property\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The tilde (`~`) prefix is intentional.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It sorts to the bottom of TypeScript's REDACTEDcomplete, so `schema.~standard` doesn't pollute your intellisense when you're working with `schema.parse()` or `schema.safeParse()`.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"const result = await EmailSchema['~standard'].validate('not-an-email');\n"[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export async function expectValid<T>(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schema: StandardSchemaV1<unknown, T>,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'value: unknown\n'[39m +
                      [32m'): Promise<T> {\n'[39m +

                      [32m'}\n'[39m +

                      [32m'With Standard Schema, a single `if (schema["~standard"]) schema["~standard"].validate(value)` code path handles all conforming libraries.'[39m

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"`arktype`is not just a validator- it's a type system.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'If we can deeply intersect arbitrary types, optimize them, and determine assignability, we can use all of that to make discrimination much easier (being able to "discriminate" is equivalent to having some common path that has an intersection of\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Most ArkType definitions are just objects and strings and can be easily serialized and eventually could even be used to validate data across multiple languages.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"|filter|apply a predicate function to input|⚠️ the behavior ofnarrow, this method's output counterpart, is usually more desirable ✅ most useful for morphs with input types that are re-used externally 🥸Type predicatescan be used as casts|\n"[39m +

                      [32m'// ArkErrors: must be an object, a string, a number or a bigint (was boolean)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'なお、ArkTypeではプリミティブな値のバリデーション定義として以下をサポートしており、これらを組み合わせて定義を作っていくことが基本となります。\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const parseJson = type("string").pipe.try(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(s): object => JSON.parse(s),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: "string",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'version: "string.semver"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m');\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'またJSON.parseについては、ArkTypeが`string.json.parse`という定義を用意しているため、これを用いると単純にバリデーション定義同士を連結すればよいことになります。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'その場合は`to`メソッドを用いることで連結ができます。\n'[39m +

                      [32m'const parseJson = type("string.json.parse").to({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: "string",\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'- When issuing multiple commands:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`).             [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +

Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'## When to Use This Tool\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser REDACTEDmation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome REDACTED-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent can analyze code and create review comments on specific lines.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "review the code in src/auth"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "add review comments to this file"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### walkthrough\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to create a summary of the changes made in the current task.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to documentation and explanation; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "summarize what we have done"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a walkthrough for the changes"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "explain the changes made in this task"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
